title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drainage Runs
description: Installing a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage branch is a frequent code violation that causes chronic clogs. Sanitary tees feature a tight turn designed specifically for transitioning flow from horizontal to vertical. When placed horizontally, waste liquid drops quickly while solids decelerate, accumulating at the branch entry point. Proper drainage design requires long-turn fittings, such as a combination wye and eighth bend or a standard wye with a street bend. These fittings gradually direct water and solids together, preserving momentum and maintaining proper self-scouring velocity inside the pipe.
